item.title: 'We all made mistakes': Darren Lehmann stands by Sandpapergate version, reveals 'dark place' after 2018 scandal
item.description: The Sandpapergate controversy continues to haunt Australian cricket, with former coach Darren Lehmann once again insisting that he had no knowledge of the ball-tampering plot during the 2018 South Africa tour. Acknowledging that the scandal was a dark chapter for everyone involved, Lehmann said he accepted responsibility as coach but stood by his version of events. Speaking to ABC Radio ahead of the first T20I between Australia and England on Saturday, Lehmann said the controversy had taken a severe personal toll but maintained that his account had not changed. "I haven't changed my views from what happened in 2018," Lehmann said. "It was a dark time, and we got a lot of things wrong, but my version still stays the same. It was just a bad time. We all made mistakes." The former Australia coach's comments come amid renewed scrutiny of the scandal following Usman Khawaja's claim that "all of us" knew about the ball-tampering plan and Cameron Bancroft's detailed account of the events in a 4,000-word article. ALSO READ: Sandpapergate fallout: Usman Khawaja, David Warner pulled from commentary duties amid fresh storm Lehmann denies knowledge of sandpaper discussions Bancroft had claimed that conversations about getting the ball to reverse swing took place in the dressing room, with bowling coach David Saker and Lehmann present. "A conversation developed in the changing rooms about getting the ball to reverse swing," Bancroft wrote. "I remember bowling coach David Saker being involved in those conversations. Coach Darren Lehmann was also present." The former Australia opener also alleged that David Warner "raised the possibility of using sandpaper to roughen one side of the ball". However, Lehmann said he could not recall being part of that particular discussion. "I can't remember being present in that conversation," he said. "But again, it is eight and a half years ago; you'll have to ask those people. That's the issue, I have my version, and that's where I stand." Lehmann also reflected on the distinction between conventional ball maintenance and what happened during the 2018 scandal. "With reverse swing, you throw it into the dirt, you rough up one side of the ball, you might pick at it; that's been happening for 100 years," he said. "In 2018, it went too far, and I'm (responsible) for that as the coach." 'I went to a really dark place' Lehmann, who resigned as Australia's coach in the aftermath of the scandal, said he paid a heavy personal price and apologised for what happened. "People said I didn't lose anything. I actually lost the best job in the world, and I'm sorry for that, and I'm sorry for what happened. That's all I can say to the general public," he said. He also opened up about the emotional toll of the episode and the years it took him to recover. "I went to a really dark place. I went to as dark a place as you can think about. item.title: Chelsea humbled as Leeds run riot
item.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches. Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London. Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment. Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon. Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period. Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman. Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. item.title: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science
item.description: COP31 climate talks in Turkey have gone into overtime, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming targets delaying an agreement. A revised draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels, prompting strong criticism from the EU and a dozen countries demanding a clear commitment to phase them out. Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Developing nations have voiced anger over the removal of a $120 billion climate adaptation funding target. Australia is now racing to secure a revised deal before delegates leave. France 24 journalist Adria Rocha Cutiller tells us the latest.

item.title: English village votes to ‘leave UK’ over migrant camp plan
item.description: A small English village on Saturday voted to leave the UK in a symbolic poll protesting government plans to house hundreds of asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base. The vote in Barnham follows a similar protest referendum in the village of Piddington in September, also over government plans to move asylum seekers from hotels into former military accommodation. Between 400 to 500 people were eligible to vote in the ballot which carried no legal weight, with 257 voting for independence, 16 against, and one spoilt ballot. “There’s an issue with the sheer volume of people expected to be accommodated,” the chairwoman of the Barnham residents’ association, Helen Beck, told AFP earlier. “Barnham is a small village. There will be nothing for the (lodged) people to do, nowhere to go.” Under plans by Britain’s government, the base near the village in rural eastern England will be used to accommodate 931 migrants. The village has a population of 584. Residents were asked whether they supported seeking a “crown dependency status” similar to that of Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man. Parish council chair John Bauer said this would allow the village to “retain loyalty to the crown” while removing itself from Home Office jurisdiction. – Safety concern – Residents in both Barnham and Piddington say they are also worried about locals’ safety, particularly that of women. “We’ve been told they (the asylum seekers) are all males. We don’t know where they are from, their background,” Beck said. “People are anxious about walking alone, walking their dog in darkness if an additional 900 men arrive in the area,” she said. In the Piddington vote in September, 285 out of 312 votes were cast in favour of “pursuing self-determination”. The government plans to house around 1,250 asylum seekers on a former defence ministry site close to Piddington village, all single men between 18 and 65. Britain’s centre-left government, in power since July 2024, has vowed to end the use of hotels as migrant accommodation following a public outcry. It plans to move all those currently in hotels — a policy inherited from the last Conservative government — to former military bases by 2029. But Beck said that there were questions about whether military-style accommodation was suitable for people “fleeing a conflict or persecution”, adding that it was also “significantly more expensive than hotels”. item.title: Mike Pettine Can, and Should, Turn Tide for the Cowboys
item.description: So, the Dallas Cowboys are in turmoil… again. In a year full of Cowboys surprises, both good and bad, the biggest one has somehow been the defense. After a historically bad 2025, no one expected Dallas to be any worse in 2026. Hiring former Eagles DB coach Christian Parker as the defensive coordinator gave the Dallas faithful even more hope for the defense. It’s now less than a week until Thanksgiving, and the defense is so horrendous to the point that Parker has been relieved of his duties as the defensive play-caller. Not a single Cowboys fan had that on their bingo card for the year. Now, in steps defensive assistant Mike Pettine to try and save the day. His mission starts on Sunday against the Titans, a game many people don’t see as a measuring stick for improvement. I can already see it now: DAL fires/takes away play-calling duties from Christian Parker, and DAL's defense performs adequately against the Terribad Titans (TT) and Egregious Eagles (EE), so everyone hurts their hands giving each other high-fives before the defense inevitably… — John Owning (@JohnOwning) November 17, 2026 However, just because the Tennessee Titans aren’t a prolific offensive powerhouse doesn’t mean Pettine can’t show what he’s got from day one. There are various ways to measure improvement, and Pettine will have to measure up quickly. Old Soul ‘Round the Block Before getting to how he’ll be tested, it’d be good to know exactly who the Cowboy faithful are putting the fate of the defense behind. Mike Pettine has been coaching for as long as some of his players have been alive. Starting in 2002 with the Baltimore Ravens, Pettine has spent the last 24 seasons alternating between defensive assistant, linebacker coach, and his new role with the Cowboys as the defensive play caller. He’s got good history, too—the New York Jets’ best defenses of the century (2009/10) came with Pettine overseeing duties as the DC. Regarding that role specifically, Pettine made stops in Buffalo and Green Bay to fill it. Both stops had a mixed bag of results. He lasted a year in Buffalo, posting an average defense, and in Green Bay he lasted three, with good defenses and two NFC Title trips. Now, he’s here to try and rescue the Cowboys. Average would do wonders for Dallas right now, and good would send the city into raptures. #Cowboys senior assistant coach Mike Pettine will now take over as play-caller, so do for the first time since he was with the #Packers in 2021. Action from coach Brian Schottenheimer after a stretch of defense he called “unacceptable.” pic.twitter.com/RDXeOPMZ2G — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 18, 2026 Pettine not only has the experience, but the success to go along with it. The city of Dallas hopes that both show themselves in droves. item.title: Cal answers Tamilo’s third-quarter surge, beats Hawaiʻi 70-49 in North Shore Showcase
item.description: LĀʻIE, Hawaiʻi — Ritorya Tamilo scored five points in 21 seconds to pull Hawaiʻi within four of unbeaten California late in the third quarter Friday. Zara Russell answered with a layup, and the Golden Bears closed the period on an 11-2 run to pull away for a 70-49 victory in the North Shore Showcase opener at the Cannon Activities Center. Tamilo finished with 16 points, seven rebounds and four blocks for the Rainbow Wahine (1-4). The junior center made a career-high three 3-pointers, including the one that cut Cal’s lead to 41-37 with 3:50 left in the third. Jovi Lefotu, who set up both Tamilo baskets during that stretch, scored a season-high 11 points and had five assists. Cal (6-0) played without leading scorer Lulu Twidale and got 33 points from its bench to Hawaiʻi’s seven. Center Albina Syla scored 16 points on 8-of-12 shooting and grabbed nine rebounds as the Bears outscored Hawaiʻi 40-20 in the paint. Russell added 14 points and seven rebounds off the bench, and fellow reserve Naya Ojukwu finished with 10 points and five rebounds. Russell helped the Bears build their first lead of consequence. In the closing seconds of the first quarter, Taylor Barnes drove the baseline and found Russell in the corner for a buzzer-beating 3-pointer that put Cal ahead 19-10. Hawaiʻi trailed 29-19 with just over four minutes left in the half, then scored eight straight points, the last two on a short jumper by Rebecca Moors. Cal took a 31-27 lead into halftime, and Tamilo scored inside to bring Hawaiʻi within two again on its first basket of the third quarter. Tamilo’s third 3-pointer gave the Rainbow Wahine one more chance to catch Cal. After Russell answered, Ojukwu converted a three-point play as the Bears stretched their lead to 52-39 by the end of the quarter. Hawaiʻi made just three of 16 shots in the fourth and finished 4 of 18 from beyond the arc. Guard Bailey Flavell scored five points on 1-of-12 shooting. The Rainbow Wahine close the showcase Saturday against Gonzaga. Tipoff is set for 2 p.m. Hawaiʻi time at the Cannon Activities Center.

item.title: Ampadu urges Leeds to build on 4-1 Chelsea win as European ambitions grow
item.description: Ampadu urges Leeds to build on 4-1 Chelsea win as European ambitions grow Ethan Ampadu has said Leeds United must build on the club's 4-1 win at Chelsea amid talk of competing for European football. Leeds produced a brilliant performance to thrash Chelsea and climb into the Premier League's top six. Daniel Farke's side fell behind to Emmanuel Emegha's first Chelsea goal, but roared back to claim a first win at Chelsea in 27 years. Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds, either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin spot-kick, before Brenden Aaronson sealed an emphatic success in the capital. Leeds had not beaten Chelsea at Stamford Bridge since December 1999, when Stephen McPhail scored twice in a 2-0 success. Reflecting on the win, Ampadu said the side were well aware of Leeds' poor recent record against their fierce rivals. "We know what the history of this game is like and what the fans expect - we know they have wanted a win here for a long time. It's right we can enjoy this performance." Ampadu says Leeds ready for 'long road' to Europe after Chelsea win Leeds sit in the top six ahead of the weekend's remaining games, and Ampadu said there is an ambition in the squad to return to European football. However, he said Leeds must remain 'realistic' in that pursuit, and urged his side to find consistency in their performances. Leeds have not played in European competition since 2002/03. "We have to be realistic and understand how hard this league is. We need to back this up next week, if we don't then this performance is wasted. We know where we want to get Leeds back to. It could be a long road but we're ready for it."

item.title: Man City stumble against Fulham; Leeds thrash Chelsea at Stamford Bridge
item.description: Manchester City’s winless Premier League run extended to four games after failing to beat Fulham for the first time in 21 attempts on Saturday, as Leeds thrashed Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. Arsenal can open up an eight-point lead at the top of the table with victory at Newcastle later as City’s title challenge wilts in the wake of a guilty verdict on widespread breaches of financial rules. The club deny any wrongdoing but are likely to be hit with a severe points penalty, and possibly even relegation, unless they overturn the ruling on appeal. After seven consecutive league wins to start Enzo Maresca’s reign, the off-field uncertainty appears to have derailed City’s quest to topple defending champions Arsenal. Fulham had lost every meeting against City for the past 15 years but got their reward after striking early through Rodrigo Muniz. The home side were furious that Erling Haaland’s equaliser before half-time was controversially ruled out as the Norwegian was deemed to have kicked the ball out of the grasp of Bernd Leno. Elliot Anderson’s sweet strike saved City from a fourth consecutive defeat, but they were booed off after another disappointing display. “Almost 80 percent of the goals we concede are in the first 20 minutes and it’s for sure something we need to improve,” said Maresca. Leeds humble Chelsea Leeds climbed into the top six after coming from behind to stun Chelsea. Emmanuel Emegha’s first Chelsea goal opened the scoring, but the Blues have now lost four of their last five matches to put manager Xabi Alonso under scrutiny. Noah Okafor quickly levelled for Leeds before Dominic Calvert-Lewin put the visitors in front from the penalty spot. Okafor delivered a thumping finish into the top corner and Brenden Aaronson delivered the final blow in stoppage time as Leeds savoured a famous win at the home of one of their historic rivals. Bournemouth climbed into the Champions League places as their sensational run continued with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest. Evanilson struck for the sixth consecutive league game and Justin Kluivert added a second as the Cherries’ winning run in all competitions stretched to nine games. Tottenham are also marching up the table after a difficult start to the campaign. Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was the star of a 2-0 win over Ipswich as he netted on his first Premier League start before Dominic Solanke added a second to secure a fourth win in five for Roberto De Zerbi’s men. Thomas Frank’s arrival at Crystal Palace failed to inspire a turnaround in the Eagles’ fortunes as they lost 3-2 at Coventry to remain bottom of the table. Dwight McNeil’s late own goal gave the Sky Blues a vital victory in their quest for survival back in the top flight after four goals were shared in a thrilling first half. Sunderland frustrated Aston Villa in a 0-0 draw that lifted the Black Cats above Manchester United in the relegation zone. item.title: FBI criminal database hacked
item.description: The FBI is investigating a reported major cyberattack targeting its national law enforcement database, the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which holds sensitive criminal justice records, including information on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property. President Donald Trump said he had just been briefed on the incident, describing it as “not good”. FRANCE 24’s Fraser Jackson reports from Washington DC.

item.title: MLB rumors: Freddy Peralta drawing interest from 7 teams, including Rays
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images MLB rumors: Freddy Peralta drawing interest from 7 teams, including Rays appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Starting pitcher Freddy Peralta is arguably the most popular starting pitching free agent this offseason aside from Tarik Skubal. Peralta has been linked to multiple teams . According to Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic, Peralta is drawing interest from at least seven teams. The Athletic MLB insiders wrote in a recent article that the Tampa Bay Rays , Toronto Blue Jays, Chicago White Sox, San Diego Padres, Chicago Cubs and two unknown ball clubs have interest in the free agent starter. A number of teams would make sense as landing destinations for Peralta in MLB free agency. He bounced back following a difficult start to the 2026 season with the New York Mets following a trade to the Rays. Peralta turned in a 4.99 ERA with New York before recording a strong 3.25 ERA with Tampa Bay. Returning to the Rays could appeal to Peralta. He obviously found success with Tampa Bay. It’s no secret that the Rays wanted Peralta to throw his change-up on a more consistent basis — which led to success. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Additionally, the potential of winning the World Series remains strong for Tampa Bay. The Rays fell short in the ’26 Fall Classic to the Milwaukee Brewers, but Peralta may believe Tampa Bay could make another deep postseason push soon. With that being said, he will clearly have multiple offers to consider. Perhaps the 30-year-old will wait to sign until Skubal lands his deal. Skubal will set the market — although he is expected to command a far more lucrative contract than any other free agent this offseason. In any case, Freddy Peralta has set himself up well to earn a respectable deal this offseason. MORE TAMPA BAY RAYS NEWS Red Sox boost catching depth behind Adley Rutschman with Rays trade

item.title: Man convicted of starting palisades fire
item.description: A Los Angeles County jury found former rideshare driver Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty on Friday of starting the 2025 Palisades fire, which caused widespread destruction and loss of life. He faces a prison sentence of between five and 40 years. Liza Kaminov has more.

item.title: UFC Qatar video: Amir Albazi loses point for fence grab, scores epic comeback submission against Alessandro Costa
item.description: Amir Albazi secures a rear-naked choke against Alessandro Costa | Ed Mulholland, Zuffa LLC Amir Albazi moved to 2-0 over Alessandro Costa, but he had to work hard for it. On Saturday, Albazi and Costa squared off in a preliminary bout at UFC Qatar, a rematch of their 2022 fight that Albazi won via third-round TKO. And Albazi did it again, submitting Costa in the third round when his back was against the wall. WHAT A COMEBACK from Amir Albazi at #UFCQatar pic.twitter.com/YgnwKfPJah — MMA Fighting (@MMAFighting) November 21, 2026 Entering the fight on a two-fight losing streak, Albazi looked good to start, outworking Costa in the first round. But things changed dramatically in the second round when Costa hurt him badly with a combination that nearly led to a finish. Albazi did his best to survive the ensuing onslaught from Costa, who poured the offense on, looking for a finish. During the barrage from Costa, Albazi then made things even harder on himself, egregiously grabbing the fence, leading referee Mike Beltran to take a point from him. One point taken away from Albazi ‼️ [ #UFCQatar | LIVE on @paramountplus ] pic.twitter.com/sF94iJMhD9 — UFC on Paramount+ (@UFConParamount) November 21, 2026 Albazi survived, though, and even took the back late in the second round as Costa appeared to be fading. Albazi carried that momentum into the final frame, and with time running low, and Albazi likely needing a finish to avoid a draw or a loss, he found it, locking in a one-armed rear-naked choke and forcing the tap-out. The win is Albazi’s first since 2023, and keeps him firmly in the flyweight top 15. For Costa, the loss stops a three-fight winning streak.

Spurs made a quick start to the game and scored the opener in the 15th minute when Luca Williams-Barnett got his name on the scoresheet. Roberto De Zerbi’s men went into the half-time break 1-0 up on the scoreline. Dominic Solanke doubled his side’s lead in the 52nd minute as Tottenham ended up securing a solid 2-0 win in front of their home supporters. Let’s take a look at how each Tottenham Hotspur player fared during the clash against Ipswich Town. He made a couple of decent saves at the back and did well to secure the clean sheet. RB: Pedro Porro – 7.5/10 Porro earned possession back once and was lively on the ball. He has an assist to show for his efforts. CB: Jan Paul van Hecke – 7/10 He made two crucial interceptions inside his half and was good on the ball. CB: Marcos Senesi – 7.5/10 Senesi made a lot of crucial clearances at the back and was tidy with his passing. (Photo by Alex Broadway/Getty Images) LB: Destiny Udogie – 7/10 He cleared the danger when he could and was a strong presence in the air. item.title: Jersey Bulls cruise to impressive Littlehampton win
item.description: Jersey Bulls secured their biggest win of the season [BBC] Jersey Bulls recorded their biggest win of the season as they thrashed bottom-of-the-table Littlehampton Town 6-0. The win keeps the island second in Isthmian League South Central, two points behind Egham Town with a game in hand,. It means Bulls face third-placed Bognor Regis Town next week on their back of their biggest league win since an 8-1 victory at Chipstead in the Combined Counties League Premier Division in December 2024. Top scorner Lorne Bickley gave the Bulls an excellent start as he lobbed goalkeeper Billy Collings from an angle on the right of the box after seven-and-a-half minutes. Two minutes later Bickley got his second as he tapped in from close range after superb work from James Sunley to get to the byline and cut the ball back. Bulls almost made it 3-0 when James Queree had a 17th-minute header superbly saved by Collings. It was 3-0 13 minutes later when Jonny Le Quesne volleyed in a flicked-on throw before Sunley powered in the fourth from just inside the box six minutes later. Bickley completed his hat-trick five minutes from the break as he smashed in a right-footed effort from the edge of the box to make it 5-0. Sammy Henia-Kamau managed to miss an open goal from a Toby Ritzema cross just before the break. Jarma Mohamed - who played for Somalia against Ghana in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier in midweek - made it 6-0 after an hour when the substitute found the net seconds after coming on. Henia-Kamau had a couple more chances as the half wore on as the Bulls comfortably went home with three points. "We were ruthless," Jersey Bulls manager Elliot Powell told BBC Radio Jersey. "There was a spell when the game was relatively even, but every chance we got really we took, and when you've got a striker in the form that Lorne's in that tends to happen for you. "Long may that continue, we needed that, we needed a win away from home, but we also needed the win to set up next week against Bognor, so I'm delighted with it." Related internet links Jersey Bulls

item.title: Man City frustrated by Fulham, Leeds run riot at Chelsea
item.description: Manchester City's Erling Haaland reacts during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Man City frustrated by Fulham, Leeds run riot at Chelsea») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Elliot Anderson struck as Manchester City ended their losing run but more points were dropped as Fulham claimed a 1-1 draw at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. After Erling Haaland had an equalizer controversially disallowed, England midfielder Anderson netted with a sweet volley just before the hour to cancel out Rodrigo Muniz’s well-crafted opener. It was enough to end City’s run of three successive Premier League defeats but left them without a win in the competition for five weeks after opening the campaign with seven wins in a row. The main talking point was Haaland’s disallowed goal after 25 minutes, when the Norwegian prodded home from close range after a fumble by Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno. To City’s frustration, the German was deemed to still be in control of the ball. The draw ended Fulham’s run of 20 consecutive defeats against City in all competitions and continued their recent upturn in form under Alvaro Arbeloa, with the Cottagers now unbeaten in five Premier League games. Brilliant Leeds run riot at Chelsea Noah Okafor scored twice as Leeds beat Chelsea 4-1 to record their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Daniel Farke's team conceded six here earlier this season. That wild defeat in the League Cup in September came at a time when Chelsea were playing cavalier football that made a 6-3 scoreline seem normal, but they stand now on the brink watching their season fall apart. This was not what their supporters were sold when Xabi Alonso was appointed amidst broad smiles six months ago. They began well here, 23-year-old striker Emmanuel Emegha firing them ahead early on his full debut, but within minutes they had gifted Okafor an equalizer, a lovely finish into the corner facilitated by static Chelsea defending. Morgan Rogers might have been unfortunate to concede the penalty at the start of the second half, which was converted by the excellent Dominic Calvert-Lewin, but that decision was not the reason Chelsea were beaten so soundly. Okafor quickly made it three for Leeds, Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage time, as Chelsea slumped into mid-table. Williams-Barnett stars on dream full debut Luca Williams-Barnett lived up to the hype with a sparking display on his full debut for Tottenham to inspire a 2-0 win over Ipswich. Roberto De Zerbi turned to the 18-year-old after two bright cameos and the highly-rated Spurs attacker delivered with aplomb, scoring on his first Premier League start after 15 minutes before a mazy run set up Dominic Solanke at the start of the second half. Elsewhere, Thomas Frank suffered defeat in his first game as Crystal Palace boss as Dwight McNeil's late own goal condemned them to a 3-2 loss at Coventry. Aston Villa and Sunderland dr

item.title: Man City boss Maresca says Erling Haaland had goal wrongly disallowed
item.description: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca reacts after conceding a goal to Fulham's Rodrigo Muniz during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Fulham at the Etihad Stadium. (is associated with: «Man City boss Maresca says Erling Haaland had goal wrongly disallowed») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Enzo Maresca had no doubt Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal in Manchester City’s 1-1 draw with Fulham on Saturday should have stood. The prolific Norwegian had an effort chalked off in the Premier League encounter at the Etihad Stadium when he was deemed to have kicked the ball out of Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno’s hands. Haaland had not connected cleanly with a volley but Leno spilled the ball attempting to gather his attempt and the striker prodded in from close range. Referee Thomas Bramall, however, ruled that Leno – because the ball was still between his hands – had not lost control and VAR Sam Barrott upheld the decision. Maresca said: “I reviewed the goal after the game. From my point of view, it’s quite clear that it’s not a foul, but I’m not the guy that decides, unfortunately.” Asked how Haaland viewed the incident, Maresca added: “When they were reviewing the VAR, he was absolutely sure that it was a goal, because I asked him from the touchline. He was completely sure that it was a goal but the referee decided for different things.” With that effort ruled out in the 25th minute, City had to wait until just before the hour to cancel out Rodrigo Muniz’s 16th-minute opener. Elliot Anderson scored their equalizer with a fine volley – a sweet moment for the midfielder after being sent off playing for England last weekend. Maresca said: “It was a nice moment for him, a nice moment for us because it gave us the chance to come back in the game. “We used him today for the first time as an attacking midfielder. He was playing a little bit more deep with us. We are trying to find different solutions, the right balance, and to be more consistent.” Anderson’s equalizer ended City’s run of three successive Premier League defeats but it was nevertheless another frustrating result for a side that opened the campaign with seven straight wins. Maresca said: “For sure we don’t like this kind of moments, in terms of four games in a row without a win. “But we also know that, unfortunately, it’s normal or it’s part of your path that you go through these kind of moments. “It’s important that we find a way to keep a clean sheet. Sometimes you need to win games 1-0.” For Fulham, the result ended a sequence of 20 successive losses to City in all competitions and extended their unbeaten run to five games. Manager Alvaro Arbeloa said: “We came here trying to win this match. “Obviously we knew that we had lost the last 20 times against Man City, but I told them that we will have the chance to beat them if we play with courage, with character, if we press them so high, play the way we like to play. “I think we played really, really well. item.title: Trinity Rodman's healthiest season yet has her one win away from another NWSL title
item.description: WASHINGTON — We've all heard the saying: "The best ability is availability." That sports motto rings true more than ever for Washington Spirit forward Trinity Rodman. After being limited to a career-low 17 matches last season due to back and knee injuries, she bounced back with a career year that included personal highs in both goals (14) and assists (10). But that's not the most important accomplishment for Rodman, because if you strip away the highlight-reel goals and viral celebrations, she said she's just pleased to have played in a career-high 32 matches this season. The thought alone makes Rodman emotional. "It makes me want to cry," added the 24-year-old. "Just being able to be available, I don't think people realize how much of a blessing it is to be healthy enough to play. And I don't think you realize that until you go through something where it keeps you from doing something you love to do." Her 33rd game of the season will be the 2026 NWSL Championship, where the Spirit will face the Kansas City Current in their third consecutive finals appearance after finishing as a runner-up in the past two seasons. But unlike the last two finals when Rodman was impacted by injury, she's completely healthy heading into Saturday. More: Is Trinity Rodman playing in NWSL Championship? Washington Spirit star’s status Trinity Rodman health is biggest win The biggest question heading into the season was whether or not Rodman would remain in Washington, D.C. That was answered when Rodman signed a deal reportedly worth more than $2 million a year through 2028, making her the highest-paid player in league history. The deal was made possible by the high-impact player rule , which allows clubs to exceed the league's salary cap by up to $1 million. (The rule is nicknamed the "Rodman Rule.") She was worth every penny. "Obviously, it was incredibly important for us to keep Trinity in this league," NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman said. "The fact that she's competing in the championship, again, is poetic given how far we've come and all the progress we've made. It's no secret that the next generation of fans appreciates and enjoys stars, and Trinity's done an incredible job of building her celebrity off the field, and we are excited that she brings that to our game." The next biggest question mark is whether she could put together a full season. Between cheering on her beau, Ben Shelton , throughout his run to the US Open final and walking the runway at the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show , Rodman appeared in every single game for the Spirit this year. Spirit head coach Adrián González said it's no secret this is "100% her best season." "Not just because of the numbers... being available, I think for me, that's been key," he said after the Spirit's Decision Day win over the Chicago Red Stars, where Rodman scored a goal in the 2-0 win. "Another credit to her, honestly, she's been working very, very hard behind the scenes... you know, being more resilient." More: Wi

item.title: Tottenham Hotspur 2-0 Ipswich Town: Williams-Barnett wows in solid win
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 21: Luca Williams-Barnett of Tottenham Hotspur celebrates as he scores the opening goal of the match during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Ipswich Town at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on November 21, 2026 in London, United Kingdom. (Photo by Mark Leech/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) | Offside via Getty Images Tottenham Hotspur returned to Premier League action following the international break with a strong 2-0 win against Ipswich Town. Roberto De Zerbi rung the changes for the fixture, due to a number of factors: a lackluster performance against Leeds United before the break, injury, and miles in the legs of his international representatives. Marcos Senesi, Destiny Udogie, and James Maddison all saw rare starts, but the real selection of note was a first start for 18-year-old academy graduate Luca Williams-Barnett. Spurs began the match in the ascendancy, with Dominic Solanke heavily involved. He shot an early chance wide, before a couple of headed opportunities came his way, with the English striker unable to get the purchase he would have liked on both occasions. It was the debutant, Williams-Barnett, however, that provided the early breakthrough for Spurs. Pedro Porro played the ball into the box from the right, where the young winger had made a smart, incisive run from wide left into a goalscoring possession, doing enough to get in front of his marker and knocking the ball home to cheers from an ecstatic home crowd. A very clever free kick routine from Spurs almost provided a second, as Pedro Porro and Maddison shaped up to take the set piece from the left but with Mohammed Kudus instead taking the shot, surprising Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton and smashing his attempt off the left upright. That scare seemed to spark life in the Ipswich Town XI, as they had their best spell of the match, pressuring the Spurs 18-yard area and pinning the Lilywhites in their own end. They lacked a final ball, though, and Spurs turned the screws back on Ipswich late in the half with a Luca Williams-Barnett double chance, before Maddison found himself briefly free on the penalty spot following a corner kick. He struck the ball well, but too close to Walton, who made a good stop once more. Spurs doubled their lead early in the second half, with Williams-Barnett involved once more. He picked up the ball in his own half and drove forward, encouraged by Maddison, before putting Darnell Furlong on skates in the penalty area. That created enough space for Williams-Barnett to deliver a low cross, which Solanke met, knocking the ball into the net from point-blank range. A flurry of changes from both sides followed, as Spurs continued in the ascendancy. Conor Gallagher almost forced an own goal, fed by a brilliant pass from Porro, and then squaring the ball. item.title: Dwyane Wade Points To Davion Mitchell As Heat’s Turnaround Spark
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Heat have turned their season around in a big way after a rough start. They lost four games in a row to begin the year, but now they have won nineof their last eleven. That includes a current five-game win streak that has fans feeling good again. Dwyane Wade believes the change comes down to one specific player who stepped up when the team needed him most. Wade says Davion Mitchell has been the key catalyst for this new run of success. “I think we all are big fans of what Davion Mitchell is doing for the Miami Heat right now,” Wade said via Wade’s WY Network, according to Heavy.com . Mitchell was brought in because the team thought they might need another point guard, but now the roster feels solid. He is acting as the conductor on offense, which lets stars like Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo play their best. The stats back up Wade’s take, as Mitchell is averaging 17.2 points and nine assists per game over his first 15 contests. The team is also 1.9 points better per 100 possessions when he is on the floor. Depth Remains a Big Concern Despite the winning, the roster still has holes that could cause trouble later in the season. Draymond Green warned that the Heat lack the depth needed to be truly dangerous in the Eastern Conference. He noted that the team is always just one injury away from things going the wrong way without enough backup options. Green admitted he is enjoying watching Klay Thompson score 15.3 points per game with 43.2 percent shooting from deep, but he still sees a risk. The front office will likely need to find more help before the trade deadline to fix this issue. Plans to Bring Back a Favorite While the team looks for new depth, they are also thinking about bringing back old friends. Heat insider Ethan Skolnick reported that the organization wants to re-sign Jaime Jaquez Jr. as soon as he becomes available again. Skolnick heard from sources within the team that Pat Riley and the front office will “make a play to try and bring him back.” Jaquez was a fan favorite during his three seasons in Miami before he was traded to Milwaukee in a blockbuster deal for Giannis. He is now averaging 15 points per game for the Bucks and will hit restricted free agency in 2027. Skolnick also mentioned that the Heat could have future interest in reuniting with Kasparas Jakucionis once he reaches his rookie extension. Since Jaquez is already familiar with coach Erik Spoelstra’s system, his return would instantly energize Miami’s bench. The former forward is shooting a career-high 42.3 percent from three-point range this season. The Heat will undoubtedly try to find more depth to support their current five-game win streak.

item.title: Man City stumble again in Fulham draw, Chelsea thrashed by Leeds
item.description: Elliot Anderson's strike was not enough for Manchester City in a 1-1 draw against Fulham (Oli SCARFF) Manchester City's winless Premier League run extended to four games after failing to beat Fulham for the first time in 21 attempts on Saturday, as Leeds thrashed Chelsea 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. Arsenal can open up an eight-point lead at the top of the table with victory at Newcastle later as City's title challenge wilts in the wake of a guilty verdict on widespread breaches of financial rules. The club deny any wrongdoing but are likely to be hit with a severe points penalty, and possibly even relegation, unless they overturn the ruling on appeal. After seven consecutive league wins to start Enzo Maresca's reign, the off-field uncertainty appears to have derailed City's quest to topple defending champions Arsenal. Fulham had lost every meeting against City for the past 15 years but got their reward after striking early through Rodrigo Muniz. The home side were furious that Erling Haaland's equaliser before half-time was controversially ruled out as the Norwegian was deemed to have kicked the ball out of the grasp of Bernd Leno. Elliot Anderson's sweet strike saved City from a fourth consecutive defeat, but they were booed off after another disappointing display. "Almost 80 percent of the goals we concede are in the first 20 minutes and it's for sure something we need to improve," said Maresca. - Leeds humble Chelsea - Leeds climbed into the top six after coming from behind to stun Chelsea. Emmanuel Emegha's first Chelsea goal opened the scoring, but the Blues have now lost four of their last five matches to put manager Xabi Alonso under scrutiny. Noah Okafor quickly levelled for Leeds before Dominic Calvert-Lewin put the visitors in front from the penalty spot. Okafor delivered a thumping finish into the top corner and Brenden Aaronson delivered the final blow in stoppage time as Leeds savoured a famous win at the home of one of their historic rivals. Bournemouth climbed into the Champions League places as their sensational run continued with a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest. Evanilson struck for the sixth consecutive league game and Justin Kluivert added a second as the Cherries' winning run in all competitions stretched to nine games. Tottenham are also marching up the table after a difficult start to the campaign. Teenager Luca Williams-Barnett was the star of a 2-0 win over Ipswich as he netted on his first Premier League start before Dominic Solanke added a second to secure a fourth win in five for Roberto De Zerbi's men. Thomas Frank's arrival at Crystal Palace failed to inspire a turnaround in the Eagles' fortunes as they lost 3-2 at Coventry to remain bottom of the table. Dwight McNeil's late own goal gave the Sky Blues a vital victory in their quest for survival back in the top flight after four goals were shared in a thrilling first half. Sunderland frustrated Aston Villa in a 0-0 draw that lifted the Black Cats above Manchester United

item.title: Dominic Solanke blown away by 'crazy' Luca Williams-Barnett after full Tottenham debut
item.description: Dominic Solanke blown away by 'crazy' Luca Williams-Barnett after full Tottenham debut Dominic Solanke has called Luca Williams-Barnett's performance 'crazy' after the Tottenham teenager shone on debut against Ipswich. Williams-Barnett marked his first Premier League start with a goal and assist as Spurs secured a 2-0 win in North London. The 18-year-old opened the scoring from Pedro Porro's cross, becoming the club's third-youngest goalscorer of the Premier League era. Williams-Barnett then turned provider for Solanke, crossing for the forward to double the lead and put Roberto De Zerbi's side in control. Spurs saw out the game to clinch a fourth win in five Premier League games. Solanke explains why Tottenham are so excited about Williams-Barnett Williams-Barnett is considered the best Spurs academy product for several seasons and Solanke admits the senior players are well aware of his 'crazy' talent. "Luca was magnificent today. We see him in training every day, we know what a player he is. he's such a talent, honestly," Solanke said. "To see him come in and do that on his first Premier League start is crazy. We'll be celebrating with him today. He can bring so much for us. "He's a great person and is obviously still young, you know what young boys are like. But he's very dedicated and so brave on the ball which is great, in his position I think you need that. And he's obviously got that confidence about him which is great to have to play in the Premier League and play for a team like Tottenham. "We can see so much in him. It's exciting times for all of us, especially him."

item.title: Flyers Make Significant Line Changes Ahead of Saturday Matchup vs. Canadiens; Insight & Opinion
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It seems like winning Thursday’s game wasn’t enough for Philadelphia Flyers head coach Rick Tocchet . After having to erase a 3-goal deficit to leave Ottawa with a win, Tocchet has thrown the forward lines in a blender ahead of Saturday’s showdown against the Montreal Canadiens. While the lines weren’t perfect, the Flyers had something good going with Denver Barkey playing alongside Sean Couturier and Noel Acciari. Matvei Michkov and Noah Cates seemed to have some real chemistry with Porter Martone. After some reshuffling of the lines, the Flyers have gotten away from those groups. Now, the Flyers are rolling out a whole new forward group, with completely different lines. Jackie Spiegel of the Philadelphia Inquirer reported the team’s lines at morning skate on Saturday; the new lines look like this: Tyson Foerster – Christian Dvorak – Travis Konecny Porter Martone – Denver Barkey – Owen Tippett Cole Knuble – Noah Cates – Matvei Michkov Trevor Zegras – Sean Couturier – Noel Acciari It’s quite a different look for the Flyers. Trevor Zegras , who is tied for the 2nd most points on the team with 15 and is 2nd in goals with 5, moved from being the top-line center to the 4th-line left wing. Christian Dvorak jumped up to Zegras’ spot, with Denver Barkey , a player who seemed to fit that 4th line so well, is now the team’s 2C. Porter Martone and Cole Knuble flip-flopped lines, with Martone now on the second line and Knuble on the 3rd. The defensive pairings were lightly changed up as well. Per Spiegel’s report, Jamie Drysdale and Rasmus Ristolainen have flipped spots. The pairings now look like this: Travis Sanheim – Rasmus Ristolainen Cam York – Jamie Drysdale Nick Seeler – Oliver Bonk The 3rd pair remains the same. Overall, I don’t mind the defensive changes. Cam York seemed to be just fine offensively with Jamie Drysdale on Thursday after the in-game switch. I am not too worried about that, as York seems to be finding his way again. However, the forward changes are a bit alarming to me. While it is the 4th line, the Barkey – Couturier – Acciari line has been the one consistent line for the Flyers. Even when the rest of the team is not going, they are. Barkey just fit the play style of Acciari and Couturier, and brought the best out of both. I thought he elevated that line. I don’t think Zegras can bring that same ability. He might add a more lethal offensive threat to the line, but I think they’ll miss Barkey’s details. Overall, I just don’t understand moving Zegras to the 4th line. It will limit his offensive output as well. I’m also not a big fan of the Flyers splitting up Martone and Michkov. Keeping Cates and Michkov together is important. However, Martone and Michkov will never build that chemistry they keep getting close to if they keep getting split up. The Flyers play the Canadiens at 7:00 PM ET at the Bell Centre on Saturday. Will the new lines work out for the Flyers? Read More: Flyers Game 26: Lines, Notes,

item.title: Norwich City side becoming ‘better and better’ says Clement
item.description: Norwich City side becoming ‘better and better’ says Clement Norwich City boss Philippe Clement praised the character and development of his young squad after their 2-1 win over Cardiff City. Clement was particularly pleased with the response from his players following suggestions that fatigue had started to affect the team during a busy run of fixtures, as goals from Paris Maghoma and Mathias Kvistgaarden secured a comeback win for the Canaries. “This is a really, really good dressing room with a lot of good people,” he said. “I read somewhere a few weeks ago that people said this team was exhausted, so they have made a good reaction with all these games in a row.” The Norwich boss also highlighted the growing maturity of his squad, with Jacob Wright and Oscar Schwartau among those to impress. “We’re still the second youngest squad in the league, but they’re getting more experience and you can see that in the way that Jacob [Wright] and Oscar Schwartau played today, for example. “With the experiences, they’re becoming better and better and they’re growing to get this experience in this league.”

item.title: ‘He’s really close’: Mario Cristobal gives encouraging update on Malachi Toney
item.description: Oct 17, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Hurricanes wide receiver Malachi Toney (1) warms up before a game against the Florida State Seminoles at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Hurricanes have been without their best offensive player for the last two games, ever since star wide receiver Malachi Toney injured his ankle in practice ahead of the team’s showdown with Notre Dame. But it sounds like he could be back on the field sooner than expected. Miami head coach Mario Cristobal said on Friday that Toney is already running about 20 miles per hour after undergoing surgery two weeks ago. Cristobal added that Toney is “really close” to returning and is “probably a week and a half out.” Toney’s Injury Toney rolled his ankle at practice earlier this month, just days before Miami’s matchup with the Fighting Irish. He underwent surgery shortly after, and he has missed the Hurricanes’ last two games. Before the injury, Toney was one of the best players in college football. He had 73 catches for 1,027 yards and 13 touchdowns through Miami’s first eight games, putting him in the Heisman Trophy conversation as a non-quarterback. Without him, the Hurricanes suffered their first loss of the season, falling 31-24 to Notre Dame. Miami bounced back with a 36-25 win over Duke last weekend to improve to 9-1, and the Hurricanes are No. 7 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. Miami hosts Virginia Tech on Saturday night, with ESPN’s College GameDay in town for the game. ‘He’s really close’ Cristobal gave an update on Toney during Friday’s appearance on The Pat McAfee Show . “Yeah, he had some work done about two weeks ago and as of yesterday he was, what, running 19, 20 miles per hour, probably a little bit more. Yeah, he’s really close, so you know, we’ll probably bring him by the set tomorrow or something like that so you can see for yourself. But he’s on course,” Cristobal said, via The Pat McAfee Show . Cristobal also praised Toney for how he’s handled being sidelined. “And I think the best part about it is that he is being very proactive about not being a distraction. He knows he’s not playing right now and he’s got to coach and encourage and push his teammates to be their very best while he gets prepared to play. But probably a week and a half out,” Cristobal said. When asked about Toney’s character, Cristobal didn’t hold back. “Yeah, he embodies exactly what you want for a teammate, a son, a leader. I mean you should see him break down the team with his, like, post-practice prayer, man. Like, this guy, he could preach if he has to or he could just stand up and just lead, but he also does it with his work ethic. No one’s going to beat him to the building. No one’s going to stay longer after and all in a humble way. Like, there’s no arrogance about him whatsoever. He’s a bad son of a gun on the field. He is the nicest and most incredible gentleman off the field,” Cristobal said. Cristobal was asked about

item.title: Tottenham Hotspur player ratings vs Ipswich Town: Dominic Solanke and Luca Williams-Barnett secure comfortable win
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Ipswich Town - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tottenham Hotspur produced a professional performance at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to secure a 2-0 victory over Ipswich Town. Goals from Luca Williams-Barnett and Dominic Solanke ensured all three points remained in North London. Tottenham Hotspur delivered a tactically disciplined performance to dispatch Ipswich Town 2-0, maintaining their upward trajectory in the Premier League. The hosts controlled 64% of the possession and generated a significant 2.77 Expected Goals (xG), illustrating their dominance in territorial occupation and chance creation. Williams-Barnett opened the scoring in the 15th minute, providing the breakthrough that settled the home crowd and forced the visitors to abandon their low-block structure. The second half saw Spurs maintain their intensity, with Solanke doubling the advantage in the 51st minute following excellent build-up play. Defensively, Roberto De Zerbi's side remained largely untroubled, limiting Ipswich to just three shots on target throughout the contest. While the visitors attempted to fight back with a series of substitutions, Tottenham's structural integrity held firm, allowing them to navigate the closing stages with relative ease and secure a clean sheet. Goalkeeper & Defence Antonin Kinsky - 7/10 A relatively quiet afternoon for the young goalkeeper, who was rarely tested by the Ipswich frontline. He made three saves to preserve his clean sheet and demonstrated confident distribution to help Spurs build from the back. His command of the area during Ipswich's six corners was notable. Pedro Porro - 8/10 The captain led by example, providing the vital assist for the opening goal in the 15th minute. Porro was a constant outlet on the right flank, balancing his defensive duties with elite-level overlapping runs. His delivery remains one of Tottenham's most potent tactical weapons. Jan Paul van Hecke - 7/10 The centre-back provided a solid foundation, managing the physical threat of the Ipswich strikers with composure. He contributed to the team's 25 total clearances and was instrumental in ensuring the visitors had zero high-value chances during the transition phases. Destiny Udogie - 7/10 Udogie offered his typical athleticism on the left, frequently tucking inside to create overloads in the midfield. He was disciplined defensively before being replaced in the 79th minute as De Zerbi looked to freshen up the flanks for the final stages. Marcos Senesi - 7/10 Senesi complemented Van Hecke well, showing great anticipation to intercept Ipswich's long-ball attempts. He was tidy in possession and played a key role in the high defensive line that caught the visitors offside on two occasions. Midfield Mohammed Kudus - 7/10 A tireless performance from Kudus, who provided the energy required to disrupt Ipswich's attempts to build play. He received a yellow card in the 79th minute for a tactical foul, shortly before being substituted,

item.title: Blockbuster Trade Idea: Wizards And Jazz Swap Two $100 Million Stars
item.description: Oct 23, 2026; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Washington Wizards forward/center Anthony Davis (23) on the court against the Toronto Raptors during the first half at Capital One Arena. Mandatory Credit: Brad Mills-Imagn Images The Washington Wizards and Utah Jazz had pretty different plans coming into the 2026-27 NBA season, but after one month, neither team is having the results it expected. The Wizards are still at the bottom of the Play-In picture at 6-11, even after getting Trae Young and Anthony Davis , while the Jazz have already lost most of their starting frontcourt to injuries and are sitting at 3-13. And with both teams trying to figure out what to do next, there could be an interesting trade involving two former All-Stars who are still making a lot of money. Davis is playing some of his best basketball in years with Washington, but the Wizards have a younger center in Alex Sarr and still need much better shooting around their players . Utah, meanwhile, has Lauri Markkanen on a huge contract, although his recent injury and disappointing start have made his future a little more difficult to figure out. So, what if the Wizards and Jazz decided to swap their veteran stars? Washington could finally get the shooting it needs, while Utah would add one of the best defensive big men in the NBA and get out of Markkanen’s longer contract. It wouldn’t be a simple decision for either team, especially with how much money both players are making, but there are some good reasons why this trade could work. The Blockbuster Trade Idea Washington Wizards Receive: Lauri Markkanen, Josh Green, 2029 second-round pick (via Jazz), 2031 second-round pick (via Jazz) Utah Jazz Receive: Anthony Davis The idea here is pretty simple. Washington gets a younger forward who can shoot next to Trae Young and Alex Sarr, while Utah gets an All-Star big man who can help its defense and doesn’t have three more guaranteed seasons on his contract. Markkanen is making $46.1 million this season, while Josh Green adds another $14.7 million, giving the Jazz around $60.8 million in outgoing salaries. Davis is earning $58.5 million, so the money is close enough to make this a reasonable starting point for a trade, and I think the two second-round picks would be fair compensation for Washington taking on the longer contract, especially with Markkanen currently injured and not playing at the same level he did last season. Why The Wizards Should Consider Trading Anthony Davis Washington made two major moves to get Young and Davis, hoping its young players could learn from two established stars while the team started winning more games. But the Wizards are only 5-11, and even with Davis having a very good season, they’re still struggling to score a lot. And the biggest problem is probably their three-point shooting. Washington is making just 31.8% of its shots from beyond the arc, ranking 29th in the NBA, which is terrible for a team with someone like Trae running the offense. You

item.title: Fantastic four for Celtic against St Mirren
item.description: Fantastic four for Celtic against St Mirren Scottish Premiership Saturday, November 21, 2026 Celtic Park CELTIC…4 (Oxlade-Chamberlain 33, Durán 40, McCowan 42, McGregor 63) ST MIRREN…1 (Phillips 70) Celtic have returned from the international break with a convincing and deserved 4-1 win against St Mirren at Celtic Park, with goals from Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Camilo Durán, Luke McCowan and Callum McGregor securing the points for the Hoops. The Bhoys looked to have got off to the best possible start when Camilo Durán found the back of the net with a headed finish in the ninth minute after a good cross from Kieran Tierney, but the offside flag cut the celebrations short and the scoreline remained level. Durán had the ball in the net again five minutes later after latching on to the rebounded ball following Jota’s saved attempt on goal, but once again the offside flag denied the Colombian the opener. Celtic were in control of the match in the first 30 minutes, with Jota and Yang giving St Mirren some defensive work to do with their positive play on the wings. The visitors had to defend in numbers to deny the Hoops a clear chance at goal. With 33 minutes on the clock, the opener which Celtic deserved was delivered by Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain following some nice play on the wing from Yang. The Korean pulled away from St Mirren’s Declan John before cutting the ball back to Oxlade-Chamberlain, who produced a tidy finish from 12 yards out to put Celtic 1-0 ahead. That lead should have been doubled five minutes later when Yang burst through on goal with the ball at his feet. With just the keeper to beat, the winger could have pulled the trigger, but instead he was unselfish and tried to square it to Durán, giving the St Mirren defence a chance to clear the ball. Durán didn’t have to wait long for his next opportunity, however, and when Kieran Tierney sent a brilliant cross in to the box from the right wing a few moments later, the Colombian was on hand six yards out from goal to knock the ball by Jacob Champan and make it 2-0 to Celtic. It was 3-0 soon after, and once again Kieran Tierney was the provider, this time with a pass inside from the left wing to find Luke McCowan in the box. McCowan made no mistake as he lashed the ball into the net to put the Hoops three ahead. Early in the second half, Sam Johnstone was called in to action after Ismael Kabia sent a powerful shot towards the bottom corner from outside the box. The Celtic keeper was equal to Kabia’s effort and got down to his right to make the save. Celtic’s first changes came on the hour mark when Jota and Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain made way for Callum Osmand and Joel van den Berg, the latter making his Celtic debut. Osmand’s first involvement in the match led to Celtic’s fourth goal, with the young Englishman cutting the ball back to Camilo Durán on the edge of the area. Durán was unable to bring it under control, but the rebound landed at the feet of Callum McGregor who produced an emphatic fin

item.title: Chelsea player ratings vs Leeds United: Xabi Alonso's side collapse in 4-1 home defeat after Moises Caicedo injury
item.description: Chelsea collapsed at Stamford Bridge as Leeds United produced a clinical second-half display to claim a 4-1 victory. Emmanuel Emegha put the Blues ahead in the 25th minute, but Moises Caicedo's early injury and Morgan Rogers' handball penalty sparked a second-half meltdown as Noah Okafor struck twice alongside Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brenden Aaronson. Chelsea started brightly by pressing high and took a 25th-minute lead through Emegha, only for Okafor to exploit their wide-open backline three minutes later. Caicedo's early injury stripped the midfield of its defensive shield, and Rogers' handball penalty handed Calvert-Lewin the lead after the break. Forced to chase the game with a high line, Alonso's side were picked off on the counter as Okafor struck again in the 58th minute before Aaronson sealed the 4-1 rout in stoppage time. Goalkeeper & Defence Emiliano Martinez - 5/10 Denied Calvert-Lewin twice in the first half to keep Chelsea in the contest. Left completely exposed for Leeds' third and fourth goals as the defensive shape in front of him vanished. Josh Acheampong - 5/10 Showed early intent with a ninth-minute strike from distance, but struggled to track Okafor's movement down the flank. Replaced by Malo Gusto in the 73rd minute. Wesley Fofana - 4/10 Won his share of aerial duels, yet failed to organise the backline against Leeds' rapid transitions. His frustrated 74th-minute foul summed up a ragged afternoon. Levi Colwill - 5/10 Kept his passing tidy and pushed forward to threaten in the opposition box, having a header and a late shot blocked. Could not stop Calvert-Lewin from dominating central spaces with his hold-up play. Pep Chavarria - 4/10 Pinned back by Jayden Bogle's constant overlapping runs on the left flank. Offered little going forward before making way for Geovany Quenda late on. Midfield Midfield Moises Caicedo - 6/10 Controlled the early tempo and drew fouls cleanly before an injury forced him off in the 22nd minute. His exit proved the tactical turning point of the match. Romeo Lavia - 4/10 Overrun without Caicedo beside him, picking up a 47th-minute booking for a clumsy foul on Okafor. Lacked the physicality to track Leeds' midfield runners breaking from deep. Cole Palmer - 5/10 Set up Estevao's 16th-minute chance, but was otherwise crowded out in the final third. Struggled to find pockets of space or unlock Leeds' compact shape. Attack Morgan Rogers - 5/10 Threaded a sharp pass to assist Emegha's 25th-minute opener, only to undo his work by conceding a costly handball penalty after the break. Faded completely once Chelsea fell behind. Estevao - 6/10 Chelsea's brightest wide threat, testing James Trafford in the 16th minute and troubling Gudmundsson with direct runs. Sacrificed for Pedro Neto in the 64th minute. Emmanuel Emegha - 7/10 Chelsea's standout performer, firing home a clinical low left-footed finish in the 25th minute. item.title: Dwayne ‘The Rock’ Johnson offers sage advice for players in transfer portal/NIL era on ‘College GameDay’ set
item.description: Credit: Peter Casey-USA TODAY Sports Dwayne ‘The Rock’ Johnson offers sage advice for players in transfer portal/NIL era on ‘College GameDay’ set appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ahead of WWE Survivor Series on Thanksgiving weekend, Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson appeared at his alma mater , the University of Miami, as College GameDay’s celebrity guest picker. Miami is set to face off in a high-stakes battle with Virginia Tech on Saturday as the season nears its end and their hopes of making the college football playoffs continue. Awesome to hear from @TheRock on how he’s overcome adversity and his advice for college athletes 👏 pic.twitter.com/qZ4su4lAUA — Kirk Herbstreit (@KirkHerbstreit) November 21, 2026 Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Asked by Kirk Herbstreit what he’d tell players tempted to leave when they hit adversity, Johnson said he understood the feeling, since he faced a similar moment at Miami. “I get that, and I understand that, because I went through that when I was here at Miami, ’cause I felt like, ‘Man, is this the right place for me?’ I got injured my freshman year, redshirt freshman year. I was backup to Russell Maryland, who’s one of the greats of all time. I got hurt, and then my career changed after that time when I got hurt. And I wish I had at least the option of a portal.” He said that while the transfer portal is an opportunity, players should pause before reacting, and he encouraged them to talk to people. “But what I like to tell these young athletes today is, while the portal is there for an opportunity, take a moment. Don’t react to what’s happening around you. Take your time. Take a breath. Respond. Talk to people. Don’t hold it all in, by the way, like I did, like we did. We didn’t have mental health education back then. We had ‘suck it up’ and live with it.” Johnson said he supports players making the most of the opportunities available to them, including financially. “I would say that. But again, it’s tough because there’s a lot of opportunity out there, and I’m an advocate for every student athlete, football players for sure, ’cause I was one, to get as much as you can. And make as much money as you can, too, as well. ‘Cause there’s a cap there, and it will end.” Johnson was a defensive tackle who played for Miami from 1990 to 1994. While with the Hurricanes, he was a part of the national championship team in 1991. He played 39 games and finished his career with 4.5 sacks and 77 tackles. item.title: Justice for Denny Hamlin? Insider Drops Bold Points-Lead Proposal to Fix NASCAR’s Chase Reset
item.description: ©IMAGO/Icon Sportswire Denny Hamlin had done almost everything NASCAR could ask of a regular-season champion. He had built an 89-point lead, secured the No. 1 seed before the regular season ended, and given Joe Gibbs Racing a reason to feel confident heading into the Chase. Then came the points reset. Suddenly, that commanding advantage was worth just 25 points over the second seed. The difference between Denny Hamlin’s season-long dominance and his actual postseason advantage has now prompted an interesting discussion about whether NASCAR is rewarding its best-performing drivers enough. Andrew Kurland offered a possible solution on PRN Live , suggesting that NASCAR should retain its 25-point minimum but allow the regular-season champion to carry back a percentage of their actual points advantage. “Say, all right, number one seed gets a minimum of a 25-point buffer, but any extra points, like if you win it by a race, or if you clinch or lock this thing up by a bunch, you get a percentage of those points back. So it’s not like a set thing. Like, that would give you incentive to keep dominating.” The distinction is important because NASCAR’s 2026 championship format was designed to bring consistency back into the title conversation. After 26 regular-season races, the top 16 drivers advance to a 10-race Chase. There are no eliminations or additional resets. Every point earned during those final 10 races counts toward the championship. NASCAR's Chase format has long frustrated top contenders. See what structural change could finally level the playing field for veterans like Hamlin. Subscribe for the latest playoff analysis. However, the initial reseeding changes the value of everything drivers accumulated beforehand. Denny Hamlin’s numbers show exactly why Kurland is questioning that approach. He finished the regular season with 1,027 points, while the gap between him and second-place Ryan Blaney stood at 89. Yet, after Daytona, Hamlin started The Chase with 2,100 points and Blaney with 2,075. The other 64 points of separation had effectively vanished. Under Kurland’s suggested model, half of Denny Hamlin’s 89-point advantage would have given him approximately 45 points instead of 25. That is an additional 20 points to protect across the 10-race championship battle. More importantly, every extra point earned during the regular season would have had a purpose beyond simply securing the top seed. Kurland also pointed out that such a system could make the Daytona finale more meaningful for drivers already secure in the Chase. Rather than having little left to gain in the standings, the regular-season leader would still have something to fight for. But there is a catch, and Kurland did not overlook it. “It was, what if you get 50% of your points lead to start the Chase? And I’m just throwing that number out there. That would give the number one seed a little bit more of an incentive to keep trying to put their foot on people’s throats during the regular

item.title: 2027 Elections: Tinubu Endorses Alli, Yayi, Hamzat
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has publicly endorsed the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidates in Oyo, Ogun and Lagos states ahead of the 2027 general elections. Tinubu endorsed the candidates on Saturday by raising their hands at the party’s presidential campaign rally held at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State. Introducing the candidates, the President told supporters, “The governor you will vote for, I will show you,” before raising the hand of Senator Sharafadeen Alli, the APC governorship candidate in Oyo State. He subsequently raised the hands of Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, the party’s candidate in Ogun State, and Obafemi Hamzat, its governorship candidate in Lagos State. Tinubu also endorsed Remi Oseni, the APC senatorial candidate for Oyo South, by raising his hand at the rally. ﻿ The event marked the South-West leg of the President’s re-election campaign and the seventh state rally he had attended since the exercise began in Kaduna on October 24. Vice-President Kashim Shettima, APC governors, members of the National Assembly and other party leaders attended the rally. Tinubu, who arrived in Ibadan alongside his wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, said he was in the state to appreciate residents for their support during the 2023 presidential election. He expressed confidence that they would vote for the APC again in 2027. “I am just here to say thank you for standing with us. You gave us votes in 2023, and I am sure you will do the same in 2027,” he said. The President, however, kept his speech brief and asked the audience to observe a minute’s silence in honour of victims of a boat accident in Ukubie, Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State, on Friday. Tinubu had earlier directed that the Ibadan rally be held without much fanfare in honour of those who died in the incident and in sympathy with their families. He also disclosed that he had met with traditional rulers in Oyo State, including the Olubadan of Ibadanland and the Soun of Ogbomoso, expressing confidence in their support. The President further promised improved electricity supply and industrial development, announcing that his administration had signed an agreement with Chinese automobile manufacturer Yutong to reopen the defunct Leyland factory in Ibadan for the assembly of compressed natural gas (CNG) buses. “We will bring industries and provide jobs for our youths,” he said. The APC is seeking to take control of Oyo State from the incumbent administration of Governor Seyi Makinde, while Alli, who represents Oyo South in the Senate, emerged as the party’s consensus governorship candidate in May. In Ogun State, Adeola, who represents Ogun West Senatorial District, is the APC’s governorship candidate, while Hamzat, the incumbent deputy governor of Lagos State, is flying the party’s flag in the 2027 governorship election. item.title: Tinubu’s achievements will give him victory in Edo – Shaibu
item.description: .Says Obi’s 2023 wave won’t repeat itself ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ABUJA – FORMER Deputy Governor of Edo State and Director-General/CEO of National Institute for Sports, NIS, Rt. Hon. Philip Shaibu has said that the political wave that gave victory to the presidential candidate of the Labour Party, in 2023 election in the state, Mr. Peter Obi, will not repeat itself in the 2027 polls. ‎Shaibu said President Bola Tinubu’s reforms and achievements would give victory. ‎Speaking exclusively to Sunday Vanguard, Shaibu, who was a former President of National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, said no elections can be the same. “From my experience so far in Nigerian politics—I have actively participated since 2023, beyond student union government elections and the politics of activism—my political career started mainly in 2023 in Edo State. “Since then, from my little experience in active partisan politics, I know that no two elections are the same. Every election has its own dynamics, its own spirit, and its own issues that drive it. Edo is not different from the cyclical politics played in Nigeria. ‎”The 2023 election was a wave that we had never experienced in this country. That wave occurred because young Nigerians were interested in who became their president, and they were looking for an alternative. ‎”Even when the alternative they later got was not fully known to them, they simply wanted an alternative—someone they seemingly believed could be it, even though they did not have much information. ‎”They were persuaded and mobilised through the power of social media. Do not forget that the EndSARS protests created room for all that happened in 2023. ‎”But 2027 is a different ballgame. First, Asiwaju (President Tinubu) is now known to the people. He is known by the young people in this country, not only by partisan politicians in the state. He has now been president for over three years, and people understand what governance is. ‎”The person they thought was going to be a messiah—they have started seeing that he has more than one shoe that he claims to have. They have started seeing that the empire he has built is more than somebody owning a shoe. ‎”They have seen that the statistics they were reading, those statistics are all fallacy, they were all wrong. They were one of those home video acting to just convince people, but because people did not take time to check and that was why that wave. ‎”That wave cannot return in the next election, because even the young men and women—when you see the Tinubu support groups, you will see that it is dominated by these same young people who were part of that wave. ‎”So the politics of 2027 will be completely different from the politics of 2023, because we now know who President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is. We now know who the other opponents are. We have opponents, but we do not have an opposition. I can tell you that for the 2027 election, there are opponents, but there is no opposition.” ‎Asked why he said that
